title: Switching Dairy for Plants Risks Nutrient Deficiencies
paragraphs: There are many benefits to changing to a plant-based diet. It can support health by offering a lot of fiber, vitamins and most essential nutrients, while also being more climate-friendly, because growing plant-based food is more sustainable than meat production.

However, changing to a completely plant-based diet still needs to be done carefully. And a study has found that replacing dairy with unfortified plant-based products could lead to deficiencies in some essential nutrients.

The study was published in Planetary Health, and used data from around 3,000 people aged 18 months to 100 years. They were all participants in the UK's National Diet and Nutrition Survey, which included four days of reports on what participants ate.

The researchers modeled what would happen if participants replaced the dairy in their diets with plant-based products, calculating the nutritional value of the dairy-free options using product labels and brand websites.
In particular, they looked at essential nutrients found in dairy products — calcium, vitamin B12, riboflavin and iodine.
We need calcium to build bones, and vitamin B12 to make red blood cells. Riboflavin keeps our skin, eyes and nervous system healthy, while iodine is needed for the production of important hormones.

The researchers calculated that replacing dairy products with unfortified plant-based options reduced intake of each nutrient — and the effect was strongest among young children, teenagers and adult women.

Iodine was a particular problem. For most people, replacing 50% of dairy with plant-based products led to a 13% to 28% decrease in iodine intake, for example. And if teenagers replaced 100% of their dairy with plant-based products, 72% of boys would not be getting enough iodine — and neither would 80% of girls.

Instead of using the findings to say people shouldn't switch to plant-based foods, however, the researchers are calling for dairy replacements and other foods — like bread — to be fortified with nutrients like iodine that are hard to get without dairy.
